about.title: Dixon Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Dixon residents rely on all kinds of products every day, from farm equipment used around Pitt School Road's agricultural land to household goods and vehicle parts driven along I-80 and Rt 113. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can upend a family's routine fast. California's strict liability rules mean an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, just that the product was defective and caused harm. That said, these cases often involve multiple parties, from manufacturers to distributors to local retailers, and the physical evidence matters. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that helps connect Dixon residents with an independent attorney familiar with product defect claims. There is no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Dixon Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California often allows product liability claims to proceed under strict liability, meaning you generally don't have to show the manufacturer was negligent, just that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer that sold you the product in Dixon can potentially be held liable, which may widen the paths to recovery.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: An attorney can advise you early on how to keep the defective item and related packaging intact, since that evidence often plays a central role in proving the defect.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless to file a claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law often applies strict liability, which generally requires showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone acted negligently. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: I was hurt by farm equipment near Pitt School Road in Dixon. Does that count as product liability?
items.answer: It could, depending on whether the equipment had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect. Agricultural machinery injuries are sometimes tied to product failures rather than user error, so it's worth having the equipment examined before repairs or disposal.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the item, any packaging, and instructions exactly as they were at the time of the injury, since this evidence is often central to a claim. Avoid attempting repairs or throwing it away until you've spoken with someone who can advise you.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected through LawProactive?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service and not a law firm. If you're matched with an independent attorney and they take your case, they typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you receive a recovery.
